slots.text: I like systems where every rupee, and every record, has to be accounted for.
Senior Backend Engineer at Northwind Hollow who owns reconciliation of 3.2 million daily transactions and cut the nightly run from 5 hours to 55 minutes.

Earlier, Kavya built REST and gRPC services at Brightwater that publish ward-level service data to 11 municipal departments. Kavya also designed the append-only settlement ledger now used by 4 downstream teams, and wrote a rate-limiting library in Go.
Northwind Hollow Engineer Cuts Nightly Reconciliation From 5 Hours to 55 Minutes
Kavya Reddy also designed the event-sourced settlement ledger, now used by 4 downstream teams, and brought unmatched exceptions from 2.1% to 0.4%.

Own the reconciliation service matching 3.2 million transactions a day; nightly run time dropped from 5 hours to 55 minutes.
Designed the settlement ledger now used by 4 downstream teams.
Cut unmatched exceptions from 2.1% to 0.4%.

Built REST and gRPC services that publish ward-level service data to 11 municipal departments.
Replaced a nightly CSV exchange with an event feed, cutting data lag from 24 hours to 15 minutes.
Wrote integration adapters for 7 legacy department systems.
An append-only, event-sourced multi-currency settlement ledger with idempotent postings and an exception review UI. Built with Java, PostgreSQL and Kafka.
An open-source rate-limiting and quota library for multi-tenant gRPC and REST gateways. It has token-bucket and sliding-window limiters with per-tenant quotas, in Go.
A grievance routing service for municipal ward offices and department heads. Piloted with 3 ward offices, it routes and escalates complaints by SLA. Built with Python and FastAPI.
A Go library for multi-tenant rate limiting and quota enforcement over gRPC, released under Apache-2.0. It has 87 stars and 11 forks.
Design sketches and a small Java reference implementation of an append-only, event-sourced settlement ledger. The repository has 23 stars and 3 forks.
Pilot code in Python for routing and escalating citizen complaints by SLA, written for a municipal pilot.
